title: Interpretation clause
description: Defines key terms including fact, relevant, facts in issue, document, evidence, proved, disproved and not proved.

title: Evidence may be given of facts in issue and relevant facts
description: Evidence can be given only of facts in issue and of such other facts as are declared relevant.

title: Res gestae
description: Facts forming part of the same transaction are relevant whether they occurred at the same time and place or at different times and places.

title: Motive, preparation and previous or subsequent conduct
description: Motive and conduct are relevant when they influence or are influenced by facts in issue.

title: Confession caused by inducement, threat or promise
description: A confession is irrelevant in criminal proceedings if made due to inducement, threat or promise from a person in authority.

title: Confession to police officer not to be proved
description: No confession made to a police officer shall be proved against a person accused of any offence.

title: Discovery statement
description: When a fact is discovered in consequence of information from an accused in police custody, so much of that information as distinctly relates to the fact discovered may be proved.

title: Cases in which statement of relevant fact by person who is dead cannot be found
description: Includes dying declarations and other statements made by unavailable persons in specified circumstances.

title: Opinions of experts
description: When the court has to form an opinion on science, art, identity, foreign law or handwriting, expert opinion is relevant.

title: Oral evidence must be direct
description: Oral evidence must be direct and based on what the witness saw, heard or perceived.

title: Admissibility of electronic records
description: Electronic records are admissible subject to conditions and certification requirements prescribed by law.

title: Public documents
description: Documents forming acts or records of acts of sovereign authority, official bodies, tribunals and public officers are public documents.

title: Burden of proof
description: Whoever desires any court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependent on facts asserted by him must prove those facts.

title: On whom burden of proof lies
description: Burden lies on the party who would fail if no evidence were given on either side.

title: Burden of proving fact especially within knowledge
description: When any fact is especially within the knowledge of any person, the burden of proving that fact is upon him.

title: Court may presume existence of certain facts
description: Court may presume facts likely to have happened, having regard to common course of natural events and human conduct.

title: Who may testify
description: All persons are competent to testify unless they are prevented from understanding questions or giving rational answers due to tender years, extreme old age, disease, or similar causes.

title: Number of witnesses
description: No particular number of witnesses is required for proof of any fact.

title: Examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination
description: Defines forms of witness examination.

title: Order of examinations
description: Witnesses are first examined-in-chief, then cross-examined, and then re-examined.
